errors.what: Foot x/y readouts jump discontinuously (e.g. x 49.99 -> 9.91 -> 97 -> -431 at 90 deg, then -265 at 270 deg and +337 at 300 deg). A real Jansen foot moves smoothly within roughly +/-100-150 mm over a revolution. This points to the solver flipping assembly branch or the foot position being wrong.

The foot trace is not the flat-bottomed walking loop. It is a mass of long straight spikes and huge excursions far larger than the linkage. The mechanism is not tracing a closed, continuous path, which is consistent with branch flipping or links that do not hold their lengths.

The leg triangle (yellow) and upper triangle (purple) change orientation and fold over each other between frames. At several angles the links collapse onto one another with the joints nearly coincident, so the assembly configuration is wrong or inconsistent. The foot at 90 and 270 deg sits far from the displayed leg tip.
